In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TNF is an essential mediator of the IL-6 response to LPS, but not of the PGE2 response to LPS.
TNF is a major mediator in LPS-induced IL6 production, and PGE2, which is also a major mediator in this process, is induced by LPS through TNF.
IL-6 production induced by LPS is mediated by TNF, and PGE2 is not involved in the induction of IL-6 by LPS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TNF is an important mediator of LPS induced brain IL-6, while PGE2 has a dual effect on IL-6 and TNF production, inhibiting the production of one but augmenting that of the other.
LPS induces IL-6 through two pathways: a direct pathway and an indirect pathway through TNF.
LPS-induced IL6 is largely through TNF, which is also the case for PGE2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
anti-TNF antibodies can be used as a tool in the investigation of the mechanisms involved in the induction of IL-6 in models where TNF plays a key role.
the anti-TNF effect of S-KP is not due to its anti-inflammatory properties, but is rather due to its anti-IL-6 effect.
the use of anti-inflammatory drugs should be carefully evaluated in models where the effect on IL-6 is important, such as models of neuroinflammation.
